identity.title: GPCR-Mediated Regulation of Cytochrome P450 Drives Sulfoxaflor Resistance in Aphis gossypii Glover.

content.abstract: Rapid evolution of insecticide resistance threatens agricultural productivity. While the fundamental molecular and biochemical mechanisms underlying resistance are well documented, the regulatory processes governing resistance-associated genes, particularly those involving signal-regulated transcription factors, remain poorly understood. Here, we investigated trans-regulation of cytochrome P450 genes associated with sulfoxaflor resistance in Aphis gossypii Glover. Our findings suggest that G protein-coupled receptor (GPCR)-associated signaling and cAMP response element binding protein contribute to resistance-associated P450 gene regulation. FISH and RT-qPCR demonstrate that DopR1 transcripts are enriched in the epidermis, and beta-1A transcripts are enriched in the head. Molecular docking, heterologous expression, and biolayer interferometry assays demonstrate that DopR1 and beta-1A participate in cellular recognition or response to sulfoxaflor and activate downstream cAMP signaling. Silencing DopR1 and beta-1A reduced cAMP content, PKA activity, P450 enzyme activity, and resistance-related P450 expression, thereby enhancing aphid sensitivity to sulfoxaflor. Inhibitor-based suppression, pathway gene silencing, and dual-luciferase reporter assays implicated AC-2, AC-5, PKA-4, PKA-7, CRTC, and CREB in regulating critical resistance-related genes, especially CYP6CY19. Furthermore, functional validation using transgenic Drosophila melanogaster expressing CYP6CY13 and CYP6CY19 demonstrated increased sulfoxaflor tolerance. Collectively, these findings support a working model linking GPCR-associated signaling to the regulation of selected resistance-associated P450 genes in A. gossypii.
